chapter: Mellophone, Brunswick records and the West End Roof
title: Brunswick session in the warehouse, the gong and the missing pianist
summary: He tells of recording in a storeroom, rescuing the gong stroke with a flying handkerchief, and teaching Freddie Newman the tunes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: It involved arrangements and all kind of interludes and things like that. Sidney Arden was hella on that. He always had to have a cadenza at the end of the tune, you know. It's a funny story, Bill, when we were making those recordings. We had one of those tunes there. We get to the end of it and there's a clarinet cadenza. Well, when we made them, I had an infected toe, so I was using a stick. See, in a shoe, open shoe like this. And I had one of those big Chinese gongs, you know. So I had to hit one lick before the cadenza and another lick after the cadenza. And I didn't have a mallet. See, so I took a handkerchief and wrapped it around a drumstick, you see. And I had to hold it up like that. The gong, I didn't have a stand for the gong. I held the gong up like that. We made that thing in a warehouse. It's a, you know where Barnett's is now? Well, you know that little place they got on the side of the store where they sell appliances? No, not a lot. It's only a, it's a one-story building. Well, that's where we made them, because that's where Brunswick bought Calendary, the billiard people, who were the same people who made those Brunswick records. They were originally a billiard. They made billiard tables. Well, that's where their, that's where their storeroom was, you see. And that's where we made the records. It was a warehouse. That was on the left? Yeah, I'm not letting left yet. And what they did, they just hung up a bunch of cloth as drapes, you know, and made the, made the recordings right in there. And so I was holding the gun and I hit it, see, but when I hit it, the handkerchief flew off of the stick. It flew across the room, see. I had to get up like this and hobble on and grab the, grab the handkerchief. And I didn't have time to put it back on the stick. So what I did, I took the heavy gun like that and threw the handkerchief and hit it. Oh, yeah. And it hit right on the beat. Never missed, never missed a beat. And another, another thing with that, with that session was, uh, Mickey Marco was, like I said, was playing piano with us up at the roof. And we go, we go to record and, and, uh, Mickey don't show up. He, uh, I don't know, he got peeved at something, uh, because I was using shock ears or something like that. He got peeved, so it just don't show, that's all. He don't tell me anything, you don't say he's not going to beat anything. So I'm ready to record, I don't have any piano player. And we had to, we had, we had worked a month, month and a half on those arrangements, you know. They were head arrangements, but it took us that long to, to, to work them out. And, uh, I said, now what am I going to do now? So right away we got on the phone, we got ahold of Freddie Newman. And, uh, Freddie come up and I'm conning the, the, the guy that's directing the recording date. Uh, that was his name. Anyway, I'm conning him, he wants to know where the piano player is. I said, oh, he'd be here, he'd be here. Yeah. Well, we're half hour late as it is, you see. So, finally, Freddie comes. And what we got to do before we can cut, we got to teach Freddie the tune. Before we could, the only one that he knew out of, uh, out of the four of them was High Society. And we had, we had to teach him the tunes. And we had modulations and everything, you know. We changed keys and all. And he's like, I tell you, these Sydney Iron cadenzas and all. And everything was worked up. And, uh, oh man, we had a hell of a time. But that, that, that, that thing there with the, which you call it, the goggles. But it's right on the beat, not, not, not a second.
What tune was that you used the dong on?

I think it was on Ideas. I think that, because that was Sydney's tune. Ideas was Sydney's and, uh, get with it was Sydney's. Sizzling the blues was Joke of Pryor's. And I tried to steal High Society, but they caught me.
